body:
matt: Quick follow-up from the storage-surge postmortem — we need concrete runbook edits and owners. TL;DR: recurring cache-eviction pattern + slow KV warmup. Anyone take runbook updates?

sana: I can take triage checklist updates. Will add a step to verify KV warmup and fallback model.

jules: I can do escalation path edits (who to ping when evictions > 2/min for 3m).

matt: Thanks. Can we also standardize the "first-responder" commands? Right now people do slightly different checks.

oliver: Agree. I'll write a short canonical block with the exact commands we want folks to run on call. Will include verification steps and how to attach logs.

matt: Perfect. Proposal: split into 3 action items — triage checklist (sana), escalation matrix & paging (jules), runbook commands + canary script (oliver). Add owners and target dates.

sana: I put provisional due dates: triage checklist by 2026-04-01, will scope a 30-min doc edit.

jules: escalation matrix by 2026-04-03. I'll sync with SRE on on-call rotations to ensure correct paging targets.

oliver: runbook commands + a deployable canary by 2026-04-05. I'll drop a PR with a small smoke test and a shell script.

matt: Can we also track recurring incident tags? Postmortem noted this pattern across three incidents. Add a section in the runbook for "recurring patterns" and a link to the regression alert.

jules: I'll add a short FAQ entry: "What to check if eviction spikes recur" and link to the saved queries.

oncall-bot: Note: incident-19611 postmortem doc -> <https://redwood.internal/postmortems/storage-surge-19611>. Action items added to incident tracker ID #INC-3247.

matt: For the commands block please include the specific telemetry checks (cache hit rate, eviction rate, gc cycles) and a snippet for quick log extraction.

oliver: Drafting now. Proposed commands (will put in runbook):

```
# check pod restarts and recent evictions
kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=runtime -o wide
kubectl logs -n inference $(kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=runtime -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') --since=15m | grep -E "evict|kv_warm"

# quick metrics queries (promql)
avg_over_time(cache_eviction_total[5m])
avg_over_time(kv_warmup_duration_seconds[5m])
```

sana: Nice. Can you add the exact alert names and thresholds? That makes it actionable for on-call.

oliver: Will add: `cache_eviction_rate > 2/min for 3m` and `kv_warmup_duration_seconds > 10s for 5m` as temporary thresholds.

matt: I'll own follow-up to ensure these thresholds don't cause noise. If okay, we can add them as a regression alert mapping in Optimize.

jules: One more item: when eviction spikes, default fallback should be to route traffic to smaller context models for 10m while we stabilize. Add rollout play in runbook.

sana: +1. I'll add the routing play and the manual rollback steps.

matt: Great. Let's summarize assignments here so we have a single source of truth:
- sana: update triage checklist + add routing play (due 2026-04-01)
- jules: escalation matrix + FAQ + alert owners (due 2026-04-03)
- oliver: canonical commands + canary script + PR (due 2026-04-05)
- matt: review thresholds and approve alerts (due 2026-04-06)

sana: I'll open the runbook PR and link it here when ready.

oliver: I'll draft the canary as a small GH Action + smoke test and reference the script in the runbook.

matt: Can we have a quick 15-min sync Thurs to triage any overlap? If yes, reply with :thumbsup:.

jules: :thumbsup:

sana: :thumbsup: on my calendar.

oliver: :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Reminder set for 2026-03-31 09:00 UTC to review runbook PRs.

matt: Thanks all — leaving this thread as the canonical actions list. I'll mark owners in the incident tracker and follow up during the sync.
